source_text: [1] Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν τὸ ἴδιον ἐποίουν ὡς ἄνθρωπος εἰς ἕνωσιν κατηρτισμένος. οὗ δὲ μερισμός ἐστιν καὶ ὀργή. θεὸς οὐ κατοικεῖ. πᾶσιν οὖν μετανοοῦσιν ἀφίει ὁ κύριος, ἐὰν μετανοήσωσιν εἰς ἑνότητα θεοῦ καὶ συνέδριον τοῦ ἐπισκόπου. πιστεύω τῇ χάριτι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃς λύσει ἀφ̓ ὑμῶν πάντα δεσμόν. [2] παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς μηδὲν κατ’ ἐριθείαν πράσσειν, ἀλλὰ κατὰ χριστομαθίαν. ἐπεὶ ἤκουσά τινων λεγόντων, ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ ἐν τοῖς ἀρχείοις εὕρω ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ οὐ πιστεύω: καὶ λέγοντός μου αὐτοῖς ὅτι γέγραπται, ἀπεκρίθησάν μοι ὅτι πρόκειται. ἐμοὶ δὲ ἀρχεῖά ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, τὰ ἄθικτα ἀρχεῖα ὁ σταυρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ πίστις ἡ δἰ αὐτοῦ, ἐν οἶς θέλω ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν δικαιωθῆναι.
pass_a_gloss: So I was doing my own part, as a man fitted for unity. Where there is division and anger, God does not dwell. So the Lord forgives all who repent, if they repent and turn to the unity of God and the council of the bishop. I trust in the grace of Jesus Christ, who will loose every bond from you. And I urge you to do nothing out of rivalry, but according to what you have learned of Christ. For I heard some saying, If I do not find it in the archives, I do not believe it in the gospel. And when I said to them, It is written, they answered me, That is the question. But for me the archives are Jesus Christ; the untouchable archives are his cross and death and his resurrection and the faith that comes through him; in these I want to be justified, by your prayer.

lemmas.gloss: learning of Christ, discipleship in Christ
lie before; be the question at issue

pass_b_english: I, then, was doing my part, as a man fitted for unity. Where there is division and anger, God does not dwell. To all who repent the Lord grants forgiveness, if in repenting they turn to the unity of God and to the bishop's council. I trust in the grace of Jesus Christ, who will loose every chain from you.

Here is my plea: act from no spirit of rivalry (Philippians 2:3), but as those taught by Christ. For I heard some people saying, "Unless I find it in the archives, I don't believe it in the gospel." I told them, "It is written." Their reply: "That is exactly what is in dispute." But my archives are Jesus Christ. His cross, his death, his resurrection, and the faith that comes through him: these are the archives no one can tamper with. By these, through your prayer, I long to be justified.

choices.why: Public records or charters; the opponents mean the Old Testament as the authority on file.

choices.term: ἐὰν μὴ ἐν τοῖς ἀρχείοις εὕρω ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ οὐ πιστεύω
choices.english: Unless I find it in the archives, I don't believe it in the gospel
choices.why: With no comma before ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ the phrase goes with 'believe'; this is the disputed sentence and the choice is noted.
rejected: I will not believe the Gospel

choices.english: That is exactly what is in dispute
choices.why: Standard sense: 'that is what lies before us to prove'.
Rare compound; discipleship learned from Christ.
rejected: according to the doctrine of Christ

anf_compare.notes: ANF construes the opponents' words as 'If I do not find it in the ancient Scriptures, I will not believe the Gospel'; the supplied Greek (no comma) reads more naturally 'I do not believe it in the gospel', and ἀρχεῖα are archives, not 'ancient Scriptures' in so many words. ANF 'communion with the bishop' for συνέδριον (council). Overall argument the same.

notes: The punctuation of the opponents' sentence is disputed among editors; this follows the supplied Lake text, which has no comma before ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.
Source shows 'ἀφ̓', 'δἰ', and 'οἶς' (for οἷς); reproduced as supplied.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] is Ignatius Philadelphians 8, not another locus. Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν τὸ ἴδιον ἐποίουν ὡς ἄνθρωπος εἰς ἕνωσιν κατηρτισμένος matches A 'So I was doing my own part, as a man fitted for unity' and B 'I, then, was doing my part, as a man fitted for unity'. θεὸς οὐ κατοικεῖ stays negated in both as 'God does not dwell'. πᾶσιν οὖν μετανοοῦσιν ἀφίει ὁ κύριος, ἐὰν μετανοήσωσιν εἰς ἑνότητα θεοῦ καὶ συνέδριον τοῦ ἐπισκόπου keeps the Lord's agency, the repeated repentance, and the bishop's council. ὃς λύσει ἀφ̓ ὑμῶν πάντα δεσμόν remains future ('will loose every bond' / 'every chain'). μηδὲν κατ’ ἐριθείαν πράσσειν, ἀλλὰ κατὰ χριστομαθίαν is kept; B's (Philippians 2:3) matches the supplied wording note and is not a wrong citation. ἐὰν μὴ ἐν τοῖς ἀρχείοις εὕρω ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ οὐ πιστεύω follows the no-comma reading in both. πρόκειται is 'That is the question' / 'That is exactly what is in dispute'. τὰ ἄθικτα ἀρχεῖα ... ἐν οἶς θέλω ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν δικαιωθῆναι is complete in A and not reversed in B. Title names the thought. Notes disclose ἀφ̓, δἰ, and οἶς.

Source paragraph 1 fully covered. Pass A and B convey all clauses: identity as Ignatius Philadelphians 8, completeness (all Greek phrases rendered), negation (God does not dwell where division/anger), agency (Lord forgives, Christ looses, Ignatius urges), modality (if they repent), doctrine (archives as Christ/cross/resurrection/faith), scripture (Philippians 2:3 correctly cited via lemma/note). No omissions, additions, or contradictions. Title names the thought. Notes disclose OCR damage (ἀφ̓, δἰ, οἶς).
